ui.branding.colorPicker: Screen-reader label for the color swatch. {color} is one of the three color names above it.
ui.branding.colorHex: Screen-reader label for the hex code box. {color} is one of the three color names.
ui.branding.deleteConfirm: {name} is the user's brand name; {builtIn} is the built-in brand (DMV VGC).
ui.branding.namePlaceholder: Example only; the brand name itself is not translated.
term.eventType.grassroots: Official Play! Pokémon event type. Use the official Spanish name. Shown in the website and on graphics.
term.eventType.challenge: Official Play! Pokémon event type. Use the official Spanish name. Shown in the website and on graphics.
term.eventType.cup: Official Play! Pokémon event type. Use the official Spanish name. Shown in the website and on graphics.
term.eventType.regional: Official Play! Pokémon event type. Use the official Spanish name. Shown in the website and on graphics.
term.eventType.international: Official Play! Pokémon event type. Use the official Spanish name. Shown in the website and on graphics.
gfx.common.cpEarned: CP = Championship Points. {cp} is a number.
gfx.facts.players: Player count in the small facts line under a graphic's title (type · date · format · players).
gfx.sportsPage.headline: Newspaper headline, printed in capitals. {lastName} is the winner's last name; {event} is the event type (e.g. League Cup) or 'the event'.
gfx.sportsPage.deck: Sub-headline when there is no record. {winner} is the full name; {tournament} is the tournament name or the word 'tournament'.
gfx.sportsPage.colPlace: Column header for placing; very narrow (2–3 letters).
gfx.sportsPage.colRecord: Column header for win-loss record; short abbreviation.
gfx.sportsPage.field: Box label: how many players entered.
gfx.sportsPage.follow: Box label above the winner's social media handle.
gfx.sportsPage.earned: Box label above the Championship Points the winner earned.
ui.common.top: Label of the box where you enter how many top finishers to import (e.g. 8).
ui.app.pageTitle: Browser tab title. Set from code when the app loads (index.html keeps the English as a fallback).
ui.app.title: Page heading in the black header; printed in capitals. The brand name appears beside it.
ui.app.openConfirm: {name} is the tournament's name (or the file name).
ui.app.open: Confirm button of the open-file question.
ui.app.loadSampleMessage: Shown in a question dialog before loading the sample tournament. 'Load sample' is the name of the button.
ui.app.startOverMessage: Shown in a question dialog before clearing everything. 'Start over' is the name of the button.
ui.app.ownDataPrompt: {message} is the sentence above (Load sample / Start over explanation); it is followed by a blank line and this question.
ui.app.tab.botConfig: Tab-style link that opens the bot's settings page in a new tab. Printed in capitals.
ui.app.tab.usage: Tab name; printed in capitals. Pokémon usage statistics.
ui.tournament.division.masters: Label over the box for the number of Masters division players. Shown in capitals; keep it lowercase here.
ui.tournament.division.seniors: Label over the box for the number of Seniors division players. Shown in capitals; keep it lowercase here.
ui.tournament.division.juniors: Label over the box for the number of Juniors division players. Shown in capitals; keep it lowercase here. Play! Pokémon age divisions: use the official Spanish names.
ui.tournament.type: Label over the dropdown of event types (League Cup, Regional…). Shown in capitals.
ui.bracket.topN: Dropdown option; {size} is the number of players in the bracket (4, 8, 16…).
ui.bracket.round.quarterfinals: Column heading over the bracket's first round of 8 players; shown in capitals.
ui.bracket.round.semifinals: Column heading in the bracket editor; shown in capitals.
ui.bracket.round.finals: Column heading in the bracket editor; shown in capitals.
ui.bracket.roundN: Column heading for a round without a special name; {n} is the round number. Shown in capitals.
ui.bracket.seedSlot: Screen-reader label of a player dropdown; {n} is the seed position (1–16).
ui.bracket.won: Screen-reader label of the checkmark button that marks a player as winner; {name} is the player.
ui.bracket.tbd: Placeholder for a bracket spot that has no player yet (to be decided).
ui.bracket.champion: Shown before the champion's name, which is printed right after it (in bold).
ui.import.limitless.done: {count} is the number of players imported; {teams} is the number of teams used for usage stats. Used when there is no bracket.
ui.import.limitless.doneBracket: Same as the sentence without bracket, plus {size}, the number of players in the bracket (e.g. 8).
ui.import.limitless.missingTeams: Added after the sentence above. The number of players without a public team sheet is {count}.
ui.import.limitless.unmatched: {names} is a comma-separated list of player names that couldn't be matched to a team.
ui.import.limitless.pasteLink: Error message under the link box. Keep the example link as is.
ui.import.tdf.intro: TOM = Tournament Operations Manager, Play! Pokémon's event software. .tdf is its file type.
ui.import.tdf.fileSelection: Label above the file chooser. Shown in capitals.
ui.import.tdf.readError: Pop-up message when the file couldn't be read.
ui.player.moveUp: Screen-reader label of the up-arrow button that moves a player up the list.
ui.player.moveDown: Screen-reader label of the down-arrow button that moves a player down the list.
ui.player.removeTitle: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the trash button when the player has no name.
ui.player.removeLabel: Screen-reader label of the trash button. {name} is the player's name.
ui.player.removeConfirm: Question in a dialog. {name} is the player's name.
ui.player.removeConfirmUnnamed: Same question when the player has no name.
ui.player.collapse: Screen-reader label of the arrow button that closes a player's card.
ui.player.expand: Screen-reader label of the arrow button that opens a player's card.
ui.player.socialPlaceholder: Example of a social media handle.
ui.player.monPlaceholder: Empty Pokémon box in the team editor; {n} is the slot number 1–6.
ui.player.teraLabel: Screen-reader label of the Tera type dropdown.
ui.player.teraNone: First option of the Tera type dropdown (no Tera type chosen).
ui.player.photoHint: Small hint next to the Add photo button.
ui.player.framing: Label of the slider that moves the player's photo up and down.
ui.import.pokepaste.unmatched: {names} is a comma-separated list of Pokémon names that couldn't be matched.
ui.import.pokepaste.placeholder: Keep the example link as is.
ui.import.teamSheet.intro: … marks the words shown in bold; keep the tags around the translated words.
ui.import.teamSheet.chooseOne: Button that opens the file chooser.
ui.import.teamSheet.playerOnSheet: {name} is the name read from the sheet (shown in bold between the <b> tags).
ui.import.teamSheet.checkMarked: {count} is the number of Pokémon that couldn't be read with confidence; each is marked with “?”. Also used after a screenshot import.
ui.import.teamSheet.readAllExact: 'Six' is the number of Pokémon on a team.
ui.import.teamSheet.readAllCheck: 'Six' is the number of Pokémon on a team. Also used after a screenshot import.
ui.import.teamSheet.written: {n} is the slot number 1–6; {written} is the Pokémon name as handwritten or printed on the sheet.
ui.import.teamSheet.writtenWithItem: Same as above, plus {item}, the held item as written on the sheet.
ui.import.teamSheet.checkFlag: Small amber flag on a Pokémon the reader isn't sure about.
ui.import.teamSheet.alternatives: Introduces buttons with other possible Pokémon.
ui.import.teamSheet.checkedAgainst: {list} is a comma-separated list of the ability and moves read from the sheet, used to double-check the Pokémon.
ui.common.pokemon: Placeholder of an empty Pokémon search box.
ui.common.item: Placeholder of an empty held-item search box.
ui.common.importing: Button label while an import is running.
ui.import.teamSheet.bulkIntro: … marks the words shown in bold; keep the tags around the translated words.
ui.import.teamSheet.starting: Progress text while a file is being read.
ui.import.teamSheet.fileProgress: Progress text when several files are read. {i} is the current file number; {total} the number of files; {name} the file name; {status} is a progress message such as “starting…”.
ui.import.teamSheet.fileError: Error line. {name} is a file name; {message} is the reason it couldn't be read.
ui.import.teamSheet.sourceSheet: Where a team list came from when a PDF has several pages. {name} is the file name; {n} is the page number.
ui.import.teamSheet.quotedName: The player name read from the sheet, in quotation marks.
ui.import.teamSheet.playerSelect: Screen-reader label of the dropdown that picks which player a team list belongs to.
ui.import.teamSheet.playerOption: Dropdown option. {n} is the player's position in the list; {name} is the player's name.
ui.import.teamSheet.playerOptionTaken: Same as above, for a player already picked for another team list.
ui.import.teamSheet.unread: Tooltip on a Pokémon the reader couldn't recognise. {written} is the text read from the sheet.
ui.import.teamSheet.checkCount: Button; {count} is the number of Pokémon to double-check in that team list.
ui.import.teamSheet.useCount: Button; {count} is the number of team lists that will be applied.
ui.import.teamSheet.markedToCheck: {count} is the number of Pokémon marked “?” across all team lists.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.use: Button, and the confirm button of the question above.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.intro: … marks the words shown in bold. TOM = Tournament Operations Manager, Play! Pokémon's event software. “Import team lists for everyone” is the name of a button elsewhere on the Standings tab; keep the two in step.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.notStandings: Shown after an error message. “Import team lists for everyone” is the name of a button elsewhere on the Standings tab.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.summary: One sentence built from pieces. {count} is the number of players read; {from}, {plus} and {check} are the next three strings (they start with a space, or are empty).
ui.import.standingsPhoto.from: Part of the sentence above; starts with a space. {tournament} is the tournament name read from the page.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.plus: Part of the sentence above; starts with a space. The number of Seniors and Juniors found on a PDF or report.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.flagged: {count} is the number of rows marked “?”.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.colName: Table column header; shown in capitals.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.colRecord: Table column header; shown in capitals.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.nameLabel: Screen-reader label of a name box. {place} is the row's placing (1, 2, 3…).
ui.import.standingsPhoto.recordLabel: Screen-reader label of a record box. {place} is the row's placing.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.useTop: Label of the box for how many top finishers to use.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.topPlayed: {top} is the number of players that will be used.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.topOfficial: {top} is the number of players that will be used; {count} is the number of players in the event.
ui.import.standingsPhoto.changeCut: Follows the sentence before it on the same line.
ui.import.screenshot.intro: … marks the words shown in bold. “Moves & More” is the name of a screen in the game; use the game's own name for it.
ui.import.screenshot.nicknames: Follows the sentence before it on the same line.
ui.import.screenshot.nickname: {n} is the slot number 1–6; {nickname} is the Pokémon's nickname read from the screenshot.
ui.import.screenshot.nicknameAbility: Same as above, plus {ability}, the ability read from the screenshot.
ui.import.screenshot.movesRead: {moves} is a comma-separated list of the moves read from the screenshot.
